intents.answer: Hey there! Ask me about my work, my projects, or how to reach me.
I'm Sahil Dangol, an AI engineer in Kathmandu. I go deep on three things: memory systems, LLMs and AI infrastructure.
I'm an AI engineer at Teslatech, the studio behind Callbreak. I build internal tools with RAG and classical ML, plus the infrastructure behind them: token optimisation and model routing.
Memory is my favourite part: long-term and episodic memory for agents, hybrid RAG/CAG retrieval, and the vector and graph stores underneath.
RAG lets a model look things up in your own documents before answering, so it stays grounded. I build hybrid RAG/CAG: dense, sparse and cache-augmented retrieval.
Yes. I adapt open models with LoRA/QLoRA, wire them into agentic workflows with LangGraph, and use evals to check they actually got better.
They can. I quantise models (GGUF, AWQ) so they run on local hardware, then route only the hard tasks to bigger hosted models.
A router reads each request and sends it to the best model for the job: a fast local model for simple work, a bigger one only when it's needed. Cheaper and quicker.
I cut tokens and cost with routing, caching and leaner prompts, and keep serving fast under load with queues and good observability.
A few favourites: AutoTFT, financial forecasting with Temporal Fusion Transformers; an Agentic AI Therapist with privacy-first retrieval; and Titan City, a NASA Space Apps national winner.
AI engineer at Teslatech since November 2026. Before that I was a software engineer at Asteroid Studio in Lalitpur, building accounting and IoT systems.
I'm president of KathFOSS, the Kathford FOSS Community, with 100+ active contributors. We run workshops, hackathons and contributor programs.
Day to day: Python, TypeScript, PyTorch, LangGraph, FastAPI, Node.js, PostgreSQL, Redis, Docker and Kafka.
I'm studying Computer Engineering at Kathford International College (Tribhuvan University), 2023–2027, and I hold a Rice University specialization in engineering project management.
Yes! I'm open to AI engineering roles, collaborations and open-source work. Want to send me a message?
The quickest way is the message form, or email dangolsahil2005@gmail.com. I'm on LinkedIn too.
Anytime! Anything else you'd like to know?

engineering.heading: AI engineer. End to end.
engineering.intro: I build everything from data pipelines to product UI, but three things are where I go deep: how models remember, how they're shaped, and how they run.

chapters.title: Memory systems
chapters.tagline: Giving LLMs a memory worth having.
chapters.description: Agents that remember the right things, forget the rest, and recall it in milliseconds. I design short- and long-term memory, hybrid RAG/CAG retrieval, and the vector and graph stores underneath.
points: Long-term and episodic memory for agents
Hybrid retrieval: dense, sparse and cache-augmented
Vector + graph stores, chunking and re-ranking

chapters.title: LLMs
chapters.description: From prompt to fine-tune to production agent. I adapt open models with LoRA/QLoRA, quantise them to run anywhere, wire them into agentic workflows, and measure whether they actually got better.
points: Agentic workflows with LangGraph, plus evals

chapters.title: AI infrastructure
chapters.description: The systems that make AI affordable at scale: routers that send each task to the right model, local or hosted, token optimisation that cuts cost without losing quality, and serving that stays fast under load.
points: Task-based routing across local and hosted models
